_severity: MAJOR = worse past the parity margin. minor = worse, but inside the band where two correct parsers are expected to disagree; still recorded, because a corpus-wide drift of small regressions is what a per-document margin is blind to. Refusal-tier documents are ranked above every metric verdict: a changed refusal is a changed API.

sampling._note: Why the shipping profile was sampled on the expansion corpus and measured in full on the gated 16.

measured.real_world_3: y03_nist_fips197 (46p), y10_nist_fips180 (36p), y13_irs_pub501 (31p, designed_stress). Real-world documents, one from the stress tier, chosen as the three largest that still fit the budget.
measured.stress_1: y06_irs_1040_instructions (126p, designed_stress). Added deliberately after the first results came in, because y13 alone would have left the designed_stress tier represented by a single document at this profile, and it is the largest document measured here.
measured.synthetic_all_16: x01..x16 -- every synthetic expansion document, 31 pages total. Chosen in full because they cover all four generator dialects (LibreOffice, Chromium/Skia, ReportLab, fpdf2) at negligible cost, and dialect coverage is what the shipping profile had never been tested against.

not_measured_at_this_profile.honest_caveat: This is the sample's real weakness. The excluded documents are exactly the long real-world ones where a refinement loop has the most pages over which to diverge, and all 6 are measured at the candidate profile only. The shipping-profile finding therefore rests on 20 of 26 measurable documents and 270 of 841 pages. It is directionally strong because the gated 16 show the same effect independently and because the two tiers agree, but it is not corpus-complete and must not be quoted as if it were.
not_measured_at_this_profile.why: 6 long real-world documents carrying 571 of the corpus's 841 measurable pages (68%). Excluded on cost alone, not on any expectation about their result.

sampling.reason: refine3 runs the LibreOffice feedback loop three times per document per arm, so cost scales with pages x rounds x 2 backends. The gated 16 at this profile took ~20 minutes; the 26 measurable expansion documents carry 841 source pages against the gated corpus's ~60, so the full matrix did not fit the budget.

gated16_candidate._note: The gated 16 at the Google-proven candidate profile. Reproduces the picture parity_policy.json is bound to: 7 raw regressions, matching that policy's own `_not_recorded_here` note (8 before c1cbc2a retired c2_paper2col).

gated16_product._note: The gated 16 at the SHIPPING profile: pymupdf/standard/libreoffice/refine3@240dpi against pdfium/standard/libreoffice/refine3@240dpi. The migration swaps the core backend under exactly this profile. No committed policy is bound to it, so the run is unadjudicated by construction and exits 2.

_diagnosis._note: A first hypothesis -- that LibreOffice chokes on the PDFium DOCX -- was tested directly and is FALSE. It is recorded here because the correct answer is more damaging, and because the wrong one would have blamed the oracle.
_diagnosis.actual_cause: The kill is in scoring, not rendering. `harness.evaluate` rasterises every page of both sides, so its cost scales with the OUTPUT page count -- and the output page counts are not comparable: y02 is 114 source pages and renders to 173 pages under PyMuPDF against 615 under PDFium (3.6x the incumbent, 5.4x the source); y06 is 126 source pages and renders to 309 against 576.
_diagnosis.not_fixed_here: Reported, not fixed: this runner measures, and the cause lies in product code.
_diagnosis.render_probe: soffice was run by hand on all four DOCX, outside the parity harness, sampling RSS from /proc. All four rendered successfully: peak RSS 227 MB (pymupdf y02), 289 MB (pdfium y02), 475 MB (pymupdf y06), 437 MB (pdfium y06). The render is cheap and symmetric.
_diagnosis.why_it_matters: These two documents are therefore not unmeasurable for an infrastructure reason that a bigger machine would fix. They are unmeasurable BECAUSE the candidate output is inflated far enough to exhaust 15.6 GB, and that inflation is the same defect the measured documents report as page_err: y01 +25 -> +159, y09 +6 -> +60, y17 +25 -> +105. A 114-page standards document becoming a 615-page DOCX is a product failure, not a metric nudge.

unmeasured_documents._what_this_section_is: Two documents produced no comparison. They are recorded here rather than left absent, because a document with no row is not a document with nothing to say about it -- and in this case the reason it has no row IS the finding.
